### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **38** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-storage/README.md`, `packages/services/service-storage/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-storage/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via maxUploadMb (symbol, a field of interface MountStorageRoutesOptions; a field of interface StorageLimitHostOptions; a field of interface StorageRoutesComposition; a field of interface StorageRoutesOptions; a field of interface StorageServicePluginOptions))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via mountStorageRoutes (symbol, a top-level function), mountStorageRoutes (literal, a string literal in mountStorageRoutes))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-storage/README.md`, `packages/services/service-storage/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-storage/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `66105c838e91ee6685b63ccb11ac15fe6e74583a` — the merge of head `667098ef47ac71cd5f4e24aaabebf0255f8c1538` into base `895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 66105c838e91ee6685b63ccb11ac15fe6e74583a && git checkout 66105c838e91ee6685b63ccb11ac15fe6e74583a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87 667098ef47ac71cd5f4e24aaabebf0255f8c1538 && git checkout -B drift-repro 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87 && git merge --no-ff 667098ef47ac71cd5f4e24aaabebf0255f8c1538

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `14805de73571f1c52f575e821fbfcb72b5f1be0d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-limits.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/mount-storage-routes.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/field-file-service.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-attachment-service.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/record-file-access.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-limits.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/record-file-access.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/README.md, packages/services/service-storage/package.json, packages/services/service-storage/vitest.config.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/request-body-limit-upload-doors.dogfood.test.ts, pnpm-lock.yaml + packages/services/service-storage/src/swappable-storage-service.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/storage.manifest.ts, packages/services/service-settings/package.json, packages/core/src/capability-composition.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-dev/src/dev-plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/data-migration-plugins.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts (cited code, read at the head, not reviewed); the two prose-face files (.changeset/storage-upload-bound-built-in-default.md, content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx) were read for what they declare.

Read at 2026-11-15T14:08Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6895465109. The lane handed it to review#1 (6895325870), which signed off; review#2 took it as the seated review seat. Independence: implemented and dispatched by security#1 (sunhaolin); reviewed by os-tesla.

No path of the diff is a published schema (nothing under `packages/spec/src`) and none is a governed surface (Prime Directive #14 register). The face is the declared narrowing alone.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes, each read in the tree at the head:

- **Unset upload bound resolves to 100 MB, never to no bound** (`resolveStorageLimits`, layer 4 is `DEFAULT_MAX_UPLOAD_MB`). Right. It is the declared narrowing. On `main` the same call with no snapshot answered no bound.
- **A saved value that is present but not a positive number now falls to the host option or the built-in bound.** Right, and declared (changeset "Failure paths"). On `main` that dropped value resolved to no bound. See S1: the "Who moves" list omits this host.
- **A settings read that fails lands on a bound.** Right, declared.
- **New optional host option `maxUploadMb`** on `StorageServicePluginOptions`, `MountStorageRoutesOptions`, `StorageRoutesOptions` and `StorageRoutesComposition`: a positive finite number or the one spelling `'unlimited'`. Right: additive, and it enters through the same layer function the two TTLs use.
- **Construction, mount and route registration now throw on any other `maxUploadMb`.** Right, declared. The key was undeclared before, so a host that passed one was ignored and is now refused; that is the declared refusal, not a hidden one.
- **A saved setting still wins over every host choice, `'unlimited'` included.** Right, and pinned.
- **Server-side file verbs take the plugin's host option** (`hostMaxUploadMb` on the three deps interfaces). Right: optional and additive; absent it resolves to the namespace default or the built-in bound, so a caller that constructs these services itself is bounded, never unbounded.
- **`ResolvedStorageLimits` gains `maxUploadLayer`.** Right: the type is not exported from the package entry, so no consumer constructs it.
- **Refusal message and boot line.** Additive text; right.
- **Unchanged, verified:** a settings-bound host with nothing saved resolves to the manifest default 100 MB before and after; the manifest (`storage.manifest.ts`: default 100, scope global, platform-admin write) is untouched; both TTL resolutions are value-identical to `main`.

Is the declared narrowing the whole narrowing? In the code, yes: every read of the resolved bound in non-test source (`storage-routes.ts`, `field-file-service.ts`, `file-attachment-service.ts`, `record-file-access.ts`, the two boot lines) goes through `resolveStorageLimits`, and I found no configuration or request whose behaviour changes outside the classes above. In the declaration, one moved class is named in the rule text but left out of the "Who moves" list (S1).

Is "one precedence" one across every upload door? The order is one: a single `pickLayer`, called for all three keys, and every door and verb resolves through it per request. The host layer, though, is per composition: the plugin's own mount and the kernel verbs read the plugin's option, a `mountStorageRoutes` mount reads its own. Where the two differ the byte doors and the verbs resolve different bounds; on the upload-link spend the tighter one decides. The tree says so in the `MountStorageRoutesOptions.maxUploadMb` jsdoc and the changeset tells the host to pass both, and the TTLs already behave this way, so I name it and do not grade it.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/service-storage` at `patch`, summary `fix(service-storage)!:`. AGENTS.md (Pre-push step 3) ships a non-protocol breaking change at `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The banner is there, the body carries the from/to and a one-line remedy, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker is present: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. That arm is right: no authorable key, no stored row and no manifest value changes, so there is nothing for a metadata migration to rewrite.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: present line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body, and correct. No published schema moves; the accept set of a host composition narrows.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: correct. Nothing a metadata author can write is added, refused or re-meant; `max_upload_mb` keeps its key, type, bounds and declared default, and the new option is host code.
- `dependencies` label: the one dependency change is `@objectstack/service-settings` as a `workspace:*` devDependency of service-storage (package.json, three lockfile lines, one vitest source alias). It is test-only, used by the drift pin that holds the built-in bound equal to the manifest default, and read from source for the reason the neighbouring aliases give. service-settings does not depend on service-storage, so no cycle. Justified; nothing new is published as a runtime dependency.
- Check-runs on this head: 78 runs, all completed. 62 success, 15 skipped, 1 cancelled. The cancelled one is a `Check Changeset` run superseded by a later `Check Changeset` run on the same head that concluded success (an earlier one had also concluded success). No failure, nothing still running. Skipped by name include `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `UI Published Artifacts`, the two opt-in harnesses, `Queue verdict` and `Borrowed queue verdict`; none of them rendered a verdict on this head, so the dogfood reading in the PR body is the dev's local run, not a gate verdict.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `packages/spec` path, no governed surface, no `content/docs/releases` edit. The released 18.5.0 entry is left as released and the new changeset states which sentence of it no longer holds.
- The package entry (`src/index.ts`) is untouched: `HostMaxUploadMb`, `InvalidMaxUploadMbError`, `UNLIMITED_UPLOAD` and `DEFAULT_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` are not exported, although three exported option interfaces name the type and a host boot can now throw the class (N1).
- The diff changes no door's own logic: the routes and verbs keep their checks and take a different resolved value. The other writes to the store in this package (`backfill-file-references.ts`, `file-reference-lifecycle.ts`) are internal copies, not upload doors, and are outside the rule.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the rule it implements (every upload door bounded in every composition; no bound only by an explicit host choice, announced at boot; a malformed host choice refuses the boot):

- `storage-limits.ts`: holds. One layer function, four layers, the layer named with the value. Unset, absent snapshot, empty snapshot, dropped value and failed read all land on a number. The host parse refuses zero, negatives, non-finite numbers, numeric strings, other strings, null, booleans and objects, and admits only a positive finite number or the exact spelling. The numeric arm has no upper or lower edge pinned (N2).
- `storage-service-plugin.ts`: holds. The option is judged in the constructor, before any door exists, and the validated value is what the routes, the two verb services and the boot line read. The boot-line hook is registered after the settings hook and reads the snapshot the next upload will meet. `bindToSettings: false`, no settings service and a failed binding each leave the snapshot absent, which resolves to the host option or the built-in bound.
- `storage-routes.ts`: holds. The option is judged once at registration, before a route is registered (pinned: no route on refusal), and `currentLimits` still resolves per request, so a save still reaches the next request.
- `mount-storage-routes.ts`: holds for the bound; the option is judged before anything is composed. The announcement half of the rule is weaker here (S2).
- `field-file-service.ts`, `file-attachment-service.ts`, `record-file-access.ts`: hold. Each verb judges every file against the resolved bound before the engine or the store is reached, the several-file spend before the link is spent, and the nested `RecordFileAccess` receives the same host option as its parent.
- Tests: the rule pins, door pins, controls and flipped controls match the tree. Each unset path, each byte door declared and undeclared, both declared-size doors and both verbs are pinned at 101 MB refused and 100 MB accepted; the drift pin reads the manifest from source. The flipped controls are the ones whose old assertion was the behaviour being removed, and the two "host refusal is not the door's own" cases moved to the only remaining no-bound path rather than being dropped.
- `README.md`, the dogfood test comment, `vitest.config.ts`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`: agree with the code.

Tried and held: each config source (saved, env-sourced, host, manifest default, none); unset, zero, negative, non-number and wrong-case spelling at each of the three host doors; a saved value under a host `'unlimited'`; settings bound with nothing saved; a mount over a bare adapter and over an unbound plugin; global scope of the setting (there is no tenant-scoped reading of it to diverge).

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — the changeset's "Who moves" list and remedy are not the whole migration. (a) A host whose saved or env-sourced `max_upload_mb` is present but invalid also moved from no bound to 100 MB; it is named under "Failure paths" but absent from "Who moves", and its remedy differs, because the saved layer cannot express no bound. (b) The remedy sentence "one host option" assumes the host writes the constructor call; a DevPlugin-composed server does not (`dev-plugin.ts` constructs the plugin with no options), so that row needs its actual steps (turn the DevPlugin storage toggle off and mount the plugin itself, as `os serve` already lets an explicit `plugins` instance win).

S2 (should-fix) — the rule "no bound is announced at `warn` at boot" is kept by the plugin and not at every host door that accepts `'unlimited'`: `mountStorageRoutes` announces only when the host passes a `logger`, and `registerStorageRoutes`, which the changeset lists as taking the option, announces nothing. Either announce on a channel that does not depend on an optional argument, or narrow the changeset and README "Boot line" sentence to what the tree does.

N1 (nit) — export `HostMaxUploadMb` and `InvalidMaxUploadMbError` from the package entry, as the package's other option types and refusal classes are, so a host can type the option and recognise the refusal by class.

N2 (nit) — the rule "a host number always resolves to a finite, non-zero byte bound" is not pinned at the edges of the numeric arm, and `resolveStorageLimits` trusts a host value it is handed directly. Trusted host code only; details are with the seat, not here.

N3 (nit) — `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` says the host option applies "with no storage settings bound"; in the tree it also wins over the manifest default on a settings-bound host with nothing saved.

No must-fix. Two should-fix, three nits.
